combat_history.event: No combat use; standard armament of PLAN submarines, exercised regularly.
combat_history.significance: Capability assessed from fielding, not war.

modernization.description: Improved seekers and successors (Yu-9 class) for the expanding submarine fleet.
modernization.impact: Closes the gap with Western heavyweight torpedoes.

vulnerabilities.description: Acoustic discrimination against modern countermeasures is untested in combat.
vulnerabilities.context: Western boats deploy capable decoys and jammers.

vulnerabilities.description: Best performance depends on the guidance wire, limiting host-submarine manoeuvre.
vulnerabilities.context: Wire can break, dropping to autonomous homing.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Anti-submarine and anti-surface engagements from PLAN attack and conventional submarines.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The Mk 48 is combat-mature with the CBASS broadband sonar; the Yu-6 is China's analogue, narrowing a long-standing U.S. undersea edge.
Japan's domestic heavyweight torpedo of similar class.
The Royal Navy's faster heavyweight torpedo.

doctrine.role: Standard PLAN submarine-launched heavyweight torpedo for anti-submarine and anti-ship attack.
doctrine.employment: Wire-guided from the launching submarine, then acoustic/wake terminal homing.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Match Western undersea lethality with an indigenous heavyweight weapon.
doctrine.threat_context: Narrows the U.S./allied advantage in undersea warfare in the Pacific.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the Mk 48 ADCAP, Japan's Type 89 and Britain's Spearfish.
